item.title: China's long-term care insurance covers over 320 million people
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
China's long-term care insurance covers over 320 million people The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on advancing the high-quality development of healthcare security to better serve Chinese modernization in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 4, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu) BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- China's long-term care insurance system now covers more than 320 million people, with the fund's cumulative spending reaching 114.2 billion yuan (16.85 billion U.S. dollars), a health insurance official said on Friday. More than 4.6 million people have received care services under the program, said Wang Wenjun, deputy head of the National Healthcare Security Administration, at a news conference held by the State Council Information Office. To date, 22 provincial-level regions have issued implementation plans for the program, Wang said. The number of localities where the scheme has been established reached 121, and the figure is expected to rise to 247 nationwide by the end of this year, he said. As an important part of China's social security system, long-term care insurance provides care services or financial support to people who have partially or completely lost the ability to care for themselves. The scheme helps cover their basic daily needs and related medical care, easing the burden on both them and their families. The program is also a priority under China's five-year plan for improving medical security as the country responds to its rapidly aging population. At the end of 2025, China had 323.38 million people aged 60 or older, accounting for 23 percent of the population. That figure is projected to exceed 400 million by around 2035. China aims to have the long-term care insurance system in place nationwide by the end of 2028, according to a national plan to implement the program. Provisions on long-term care insurance were added to the recently adopted law on healthcare security by Chinese lawmakers at a session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The law specifies that a long-term care insurance system should be established and improved. It also stipulates that the relevant authorities under the State Council shall formulate specific measures for the financing, benefits, fund use, and supervision of long-term care insurance. item.title: China, Laos set to hold medical drill to boost disaster relief capacity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
China, Laos set to hold medical drill to boost disaster relief capacity BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- China and Laos will hold a joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise in Laos this September, which is part of bilateral efforts to boost disaster relief capacity, a Chinese defense ministry spokesperson said Friday. The exercise, which marks the sixth iteration of the "Peace Train" series, will simulate an international humanitarian medical response to a super typhoon disaster, focusing on joint on-site search and rescue, casualty evacuation, health and epidemic prevention, and psychological rescue, Jiang Bin, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, told a media briefing. As of Sept. 1 this year, 24 typhoons had formed over the northwestern Pacific and the South China Sea, 10.4 more than the historical average for the same period. First held in 2017, the "Peace Train" series is a flagship project under the China-Laos military health cooperation framework, with previous exercises covering disaster scenarios such as floods, mudslides and earthquakes. During the 2026 event, the Chinese side will also offer medical services for Lao military personnel and civilians, Jiang added. The exercise, Jiang said, will deepen and expand practical cooperation in disaster medical rescue, tropical disease control and epidemic prevention, and "better provide quality public security goods for regional countries and peoples." It is part of China's expanding efforts to boost cooperation with neighboring countries to better cope with natural disasters. After a severe mudslide struck the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing between China and Nepal last week, China has provided meteorological support, including weather monitoring, forecasting, early warning and impact services, for Nepal's rescue and relief. The country is also providing Nepal with daily updates on the development of a barrier lake above the Gyirong Port, cascading risks associated with the Cuojian River impact crater in Nepal, glacial lake risks in the Gyirong Zangbo River basin, the development and risk forecasts of new barrier lakes, and emergency hydrological monitoring. item.title: Spokesperson says China willing to work with South Pacific countries for regional peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
Spokesperson says China willing to work with South Pacific countries for regional peace (Xinhua) 09:48, September 05, 2026
BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- China is willing to work with South Pacific countries and make contributions to peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Friday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked about reports that certain Pacific island countries called for at least 24 hours' advance notice of any future missile tests. "Regarding the test launch, China has repeatedly stated its position. China is committed to the path of peaceful development, firmly pursues a national defense policy that is defensive in nature, and never engages in military expansion," he said. (Web editor: Dai Xiaoyu, Zhang Luewen)

item.title: China ready to advance all-round energy cooperation with Russia: vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
China ready to advance all-round energy cooperation with Russia: vice premier VLADIVOSTOK, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- China is ready to work with Russia to advance all-round energy cooperation and maintain the long-term sustainable development of oil and gas trade, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said on Friday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when co-chairing the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak in Russia's Far Eastern city of Vladivostok. China will work with Russia to implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, give full play to the role of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee mechanism, and promote China-Russia all-round energy cooperation to a higher level, Ding said. Ding called on both sides to continue to consolidate the achievements of existing energy cooperation, actively and properly address various concerns of enterprises, maintain the long-term sustainable development of oil and gas trade, and facilitate the orderly construction and stable operation of energy projects. He suggested that both countries actively explore new areas and new directions for energy cooperation, tap cooperation potential in cutting-edge fields, explore the mutual empowerment of artificial intelligence and energy, and continuously expand the breadth and depth of energy cooperation. He said China and Russia should jointly promote the reform of the global energy governance system, and make greater contributions to safeguarding the energy security and sustainable development of the two countries and the world at large. For his part, Novak said that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, the Russia-China energy cooperation has continuously achieved new results, playing an important role in promoting the rapid growth of bilateral trade and maintaining the stability of the two countries' energy supply chains. Russia is willing to work with China to optimize existing cooperation projects, expand and plan new areas of cooperation, and make new contributions to deepening China-Russia practical cooperation, Novak said. During the meeting, both sides took stock of cooperation in oil, natural gas, coal, electricity, renewable energy and nuclear energy, exchanged views on future cooperation, and reached broad consensus. item.title: Xi's cultural journey through museums
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
Xi's cultural journey through museums Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) CAIRO, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- On the Giza Plateau, the majestic pyramids, silent witnesses to millennia of history, now gaze across at the Grand Egyptian Museum. Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited the museum on Wednesday during his state visit to Egypt, where they were warmly received by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife. Surrounded by ancient artifacts, the two presidential couples toured the grand galleries, posing for a photo before a towering statue of Ramses II, one of the most famous pharaohs of Egypt, as curators delivered a swift primer on pharaonic history. "This museum is a book with endless pages," Xi said. He, during the tour, also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. As the world's largest museum dedicated to a single civilization, the Grand Egyptian Museum houses more than 100,000 precious artifacts. Locals have newly dubbed it the "fourth pyramid of Giza." This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2025 shows a golden mask at the King Tutankhamun exhibition hall of the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt. (Xinhua/Ahmed Gomaa) The Grand Egyptian Museum is just one of the many museums Xi has visited over the years. Whether on domestic inspection tours or overseas trips, his visits have taken him to the Sanxingdui Museum in southwest China's Sichuan province and the Yinxu Museum in central China's Henan province, key sites of early Chinese civilization, as well as the Amir Timur Museum in Uzbekistan, and the ancient Maya ruins of Chichen Itza in Mexico. The list goes on. Such frequent museum visits stem from Xi's longstanding emphasis on preserving and carrying forward traditional culture. For Xi, museums are important places that protect and pass on human civilizations. In November 2019, during his visit to the Acropolis Museum in Athens, Greece, Xi paused to admire the relief of the "Pensive Athena," the Greek goddess of war and wisdom. He and then Greek President Prokopis Pavlopoulos explored how ancient Chinese and Greek civilizations expressed their reflections on war and their shared longing for peace. Museums have also been a frequent choice for Xi to present traditional Chinese culture when hosting foreign dignitaries. Tourists visit the Palace Museum, also known as the Forbidden City, in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 29, 2023. (Xinhua/Li Xin) During U.S. President Donald Trump's two visits to China in 2017 and 2026, Xi hosted him at the Forbidden City, or the Palace Museum, and the Temple of Heaven, respectively, using the historic sites to illustrate the Chinese philosophy of pursuing peace and harmony. In Xi's eyes, museums are not simply repositories of the past. They offer people a chance to discover unfamiliar histories, recognize common threads of human creativity and gain a deeper understanding of one another. During his first state visit to Egypt in 2016, Xi toured Luxor, a city widely known as one of the world's largest open-air museums. Walking along the main avenue of Luxor Temple, Xi and Sisi discussed the distinctive features of their two ancient civilizations, recalling their long history of exchanges and mutual learning. At the temple, they also witnessed the launch of the 2016 China-Egypt Culture Year, a landmark moment in bilateral cultural exchanges. Today, the Grand Egyptian Museum provides a new setting for that dialogue between the two ancient civilizations. In a message to Sisi on its opening last year, Xi said that the museum will leave a profound mark on Egypt's cultural history and play an important role in preserving and passing on the ancient Egyptian civilization. It is encouraging to see the two ancient civilizations reaching out to each other, with the two peoples growing ever closer through mutual understanding and affinity, Xi said in the message. From Beijing to Cairo, Xi's museum visits underscore how history can bridge rather than divide civilizations, enabling them to deepen mutual understanding and draw on the wisdom of the past to shape the road ahead. As Xi has observed, "Museums bridge the past, present, and future." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi urges greater efforts to nurture capable young people for socialist cause
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
Xi urges greater efforts to nurture capable young people for socialist cause BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Congratulating a popular national children's radio program on its 70th anniversary, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged professionals in children's culture to redouble efforts in nurturing a new generation of capable young people for the socialist cause. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the call in a congratulatory letter sent Friday to China Media Group's program named Xiaolaba, or Little Trumpet. He praised the program's 70-year commitment to "telling good stories to children," which have accompanied generations of young listeners as they grew up. Xi called on the program's team and professionals in children's culture to fulfill the mission of fostering virtue through education, keep pace with the times, tap deeply into the rich cultural resources, and devote themselves to creating more excellent and popular works that promote the true, the good and the beautiful among children. He urged greater efforts to nurture a new generation of capable young people with sound moral grounding, intellectual ability, physical vigor, aesthetic sensibility, and labor skills, who will be able to contribute to and carry forward the socialist cause. Launched on Sept. 4, 1956, Xiaolaba is the first radio program in the People's Republic of China dedicated to preschool children. It has since grown into a flagship program spanning radio, television, new media and in-school broadcasting. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
